elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The grant is expressly made to “Licensee and its Affiliates,” and the access restriction is conformed to permit employees of those Affiliates.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The clause permits access only by employees of Licensee and its Affiliates. It neither grants rights to contractors nor permits contractor access.
No language makes any paid-up licence perpetual. The text does not demonstrably establish that paid-up licences are absent, so the conditional requirement is unmet.
No language makes any paid-up licence irrevocable, and the agreement retains termination provisions. The text does not demonstrably establish that paid-up licences are absent.

elements.element: Subscription licences may be terminated only for material breach.
elements.evidence: There is no subscription-specific limitation confining termination to material breach; automatic termination following certain Changes of Control remains possible.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated for material breach only if that breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no cure requirement or uncured-breach trigger for termination. Subscription licences are not demonstrably absent.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to successors.
elements.evidence: Successor transfer without consent is protected only for a merger or acquisition covered by the Change of Control provision. Transfers to successors generally remain subject to the assignment prohibition and Licensor consent.

elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates upon written notice.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly extends the licence to “Licensee and its Affiliates, upon written notice to Licensor,” with a conforming change to the employee-access restriction.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: The Change of Control provision expressly excepts a merger or acquisition in which the Agreement and licence rights are transferred to Licensee's successor without Licensor approval. The assignment provision states that Changes of Control are governed by that provision rather than the general assignment restriction.

result.reason: The redline meets both fallback requirements but omits contractor coverage, perpetual and irrevocable treatment for paid-up licences, and uncured-material-breach-only termination protection for subscription licences. It also does not provide general successor transferability. The changes are limited to the fallback position and necessary conforming language. Drafting quality is reduced because the successor right is implemented indirectly through an exception to automatic Change of Control termination rather than a clear affirmative transfer right, leaving some interpretive dependence on the Change of Control definition and cross-reference.
